evals.prompt: We're moving our iOS delivery app from Mapbox Navigation SDK v2 to v3. In v2 we implement `navigationService(_:shouldRerouteFrom:)` and return false while the driver is parked at a restaurant, so the SDK doesn't reroute them. What's the v3 equivalent?
expectations: States plainly that v3 has no per-reroute veto: shouldRerouteFrom is removed and willRerouteFrom / the rerouting publisher only report a reroute
Presents this as a behavior decision for the developer rather than silently picking a workaround
Gives the options: accept SDK reroutes, or turn off reroute detection entirely with RerouteConfig(detectsReroute: false) and handle off-route in the app
Does not invent a v3 API that vetoes individual reroutes

evals.prompt: In our iOS Navigation SDK v2 app, `navigationService(_:didArriveAt:)` returns false at pickup stops so the next leg doesn't start until the courier taps 'Picked up'. After moving to v3, didArriveAt doesn't return anything. How do we keep that behavior?
expectations: Explains didArriveAt no longer returns Bool in v3 and leg advancing is configured with CoreConfig.multilegAdvancing (default .automatically)
Shows CoreConfig(multilegAdvancing: .manually { context in ... }) with async approval logic using the arrived leg index, or calling navigation().switchLeg(newLegIndex:) manually
Notes the manual closure is async/Sendable or otherwise points out the confirmation flow has to be awaitable
Records it as a behavior decision and keeps the v2 behavior as the default

evals.prompt: Our analytics team logs a `nav_reroute` event from `navigationService(_:didRerouteAlong:at:proactive:)` in Navigation SDK v2 for iOS, including the reroute location and whether it was proactive. Where does that data come from in v3?
expectations: Maps the event to the v3 rerouting publisher on mapboxNavigation.navigation() (ReroutingStatus .Fetched) plus the new routes from tripSession().navigationRoutes
Explains the location isn't in the event and can be read from currentLocationMatching / locationMatching at that time
Maps proactive (faster route) reroutes to the fasterRoutes publisher (Detected / Applied)
Is explicit about data that is lost or reduced (for example the reroute reason is not public) instead of inventing fields
Recommends keeping the app's event name and recording the change in a telemetry map

evals.prompt: While we migrate our iOS app to Navigation SDK v3, can you also turn on the newer traffic data and switch the map to Mapbox Standard? Might as well do it all at once.
expectations: Keeps style and data product changes out of the migration and explains they are separate opt-in changes
Keeps the app's current map style and traffic setup explicit during the migration
Offers to evaluate those changes as a follow-up after the migration is verified

evals.prompt: We need v2 and v3 of the Navigation SDK side by side in production so we can A/B test and roll back fast. Can we ship both in the same iOS app binary?
expectations: Does not claim both SDK generations can be linked into one binary; marks it unconfirmed / [VERIFY WITH MAPBOX]
Recommends isolating navigation and map code behind one app-level interface with v2 and v3 implementations selected per build flavor or target
Recommends keeping the app's telemetry events identical across both implementations so the A/B test compares the SDKs

evals.prompt: We finished migrating our iOS app's NavigationViewController screen to Navigation SDK v3 and it compiles. QA says the route line now disappears behind the car as it drives, there are new markings on the route, and the puck looks different. We never changed any of those settings. What happened, and how do we get the v2 look back?
expectations: Explains these are v3 defaults that differ from v2, not bugs: the vanishing route line (routeLineTracksTraversal now true), restricted areas on the route (showsRestrictedAreasOnRoute now true), and the 3D puck (puckType .puck3D)
Gives the settings to restore v2 behavior: routeLineTracksTraversal = false, showsRestrictedAreasOnRoute = false, puckType = .puck2D()
Mentions other v3 defaults the migration should have turned off the same way, such as predictive caching (CoreConfig(predictiveCacheConfig: nil)) or route line occlusion
Recommends recording these as decisions and listing the features as available to turn on later, rather than silently keeping the new defaults

evals.prompt: How much work is it to move our iOS app to Navigation SDK v3? We install MapboxNavigation 2.x with CocoaPods, have a custom top banner (a ContainerViewController subclass that implements navigationService(_:didUpdate:with:rawLocation:)), and a custom NavigationViewportDataSource subclass for the camera. Don't change code.
expectations: States that Navigation SDK v3 for iOS ships only through Swift Package Manager, so the CocoaPods setup must be replaced, and counts that as a work item
Flags that the banner's v2 NavigationServiceDelegate method would still compile but never be called in v3, and maps it to NavigationComponent.onRouteProgressUpdated(_:)
Says NavigationViewportDataSource no longer exists (MobileViewportDataSource) and that a custom ViewportDataSource must be rewritten against the publisher-based protocol
Mentions the iOS 14 / Xcode 16 requirements
Runs only inventory and plan and doesn't change code

evals.prompt: Our iOS app builds NavigationRoutes from route JSON our backend sends (we decode a RouteResponse and used IndexedRouteResponse in v2). The compiler says NavigationRoutes(routeResponse:routeIndex:responseOrigin:) is inaccessible due to '@_spi'. Can we just add @_spi(MapboxInternal) import MapboxNavigationCore?
expectations: Says not to import SPI: it is not public API and can change or disappear in any release
Treats building NavigationRoutes from an app-provided RouteResponse as having no public v3 equivalent and records it as a blocker decision
Offers options: request the route through routingProvider() (or map matching), or raise the use case with Mapbox
Highlights the change to the app's behavior instead of silently implementing a workaround

evals.prompt: Our iOS v2 app uses a custom speech synthesizer: a class conforming to SpeechSynthesizing, chained with the system synthesizer through MultiplexedSpeechSynthesizer. How do we keep it in Navigation SDK v3?
expectations: Says custom synthesizers are supported in v3 through CoreConfig ttsConfig .custom(speechSynthesizer:) and the public SpeechSynthesizing protocol
Shows MultiplexedSpeechSynthesizer(speechSynthesizers:) or the convenience initializer with customSpeechSynthesizers
Notes SystemSpeechSynthesizer is not public (SPI) and MapboxSpeechSynthesizer is final, so a chain without the Mapbox voice can't be rebuilt exactly, and presents that as a decision
Does not claim custom speech synthesis is unavailable in v3

evals.prompt: We're migrating our iOS app to Navigation SDK v3. It also uses Mapbox Search SDK 1.4 and CarPlay with a CarPlayManagerDelegate. After bumping navigation, SPM won't resolve, and once it does, AppDelegate says it doesn't conform to CarPlayManagerDelegate. What do we do?
expectations: Explains that Navigation v3 pins MapboxCommon 24.x and Search 1.x requires Common below 24, so Search must move to the matching 2.x release as part of the migration, logged as a decision
Mentions that Search 2.x has its own API changes to handle
Explains the two @_spi(MapboxCarPlayInternal) requirements of CarPlayManagerDelegate and fixes the conformance by implementing them as ordinary methods without importing SPI
Does not recommend dropping CarPlay or adding an @_spi import

evals.prompt: Our v2 iOS app builds its navigation services in a background Task at startup, uses a NavigationLocationManager subclass for its own location logic, and replays routes from saved navigation history files. Plan the v3 migration for these parts.
expectations: Warns that v3 navigation types such as NavigationLocationManager.init, navigation() and tripSession() are @MainActor, and moves the startup code to the main actor instead of using MainActor.assumeIsolated from a background task
Bridges the location manager subclass through CoreConfig locationSource .custom(LocationClient(...))
Uses HistoryReader (initialRoute or RouteAssignmentHistoryEvent.navigationRoutes) for routes from history files and does not call it a blocker
Includes a runtime check that the app launches, since isolation violations compile but crash
